symptom: `alter snippet M.S { replace <w> with { combobox x (Attribute: $Asset.Asset_Customer, CaptionAttribute: …) } }` — check: "Check passed!"; exec: "property attributeEnumeration binds Asset_Customer, which is an association … not an attribute". The same combo box in CREATE SNIPPET, and `Attribute: Asset_Customer` inside a data view, passed check too
cause: exec's #830 refusal (`rejectAssociationAsAttribute`) lives in the widget engine's Attribute mapping; no check pass ever called it. The pluggable attribute-scope walk (#647) skips any value containing `.`/`$` (`misboundAttributeError`), and ALTER's INSERT/REPLACE widgets were never scope-checked at all
insight: exec was the right side: with no `DataSource:` a combo box is in enumeration mode and `attributeEnumeration` cannot hold a reference. check now calls exec's function with exec's entity (the parameter's for `$P.Name`, the #647 binding scope otherwise; for ALTER the stored document's ParamScope + alterEntityContext), so the two cannot drift. The combo box gets its own remedy — the generic one pointed at a grid column/drop-down filter — naming the association mode that builds: `Attribute: $Asset.M.Asset_Customer, DataSource: …` (0 errors on mx 11.6.6; `Association: $Asset.…` is refused by MDL-WIDGET42, so do not suggest that spelling). A refusal that lives only in a builder is a check gap by construction: grep each `NewValidation` in widget_engine.go for a check-time caller
